driver.description: Audio driver backend (e.g., 'alsa', 'firewire', 'dummy', 'net'). Choose based on your hardware.

device.description: Device name (e.g., 'hw:0' for ALSA). Leave empty for default device.

rate.description: Sample rate in Hz. Common values: 44100, 48000, 96000. Match your audio interface's supported rate.

period.description: Period size (frames per period). Lower = lower latency but higher CPU load. Must be a power of 2 (e.g., 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048).

nperiods.description: Number of periods in the buffer. Usually 2 or 3. Higher values may improve robustness but increase latency.

input_channels.description: Number of input channels. Set to 0 to disable capture, or match your interface's physical inputs.

output_channels.description: Number of output channels. Set to 0 to disable playback, or match your interface's physical outputs.

realtime_priority.description: Real-time priority (1–99). Higher values increase priority but may starve other processes. JACK typically works well at 5–15.

extra_args.description: Additional command-line arguments (e.g., ['--sync'] for ALSA sync mode, or ['-r'] for resampling). One argument per list item (include leading hyphen).

start_delay.description: Seconds to wait before starting JACK (for system boot-time delays).

auto_connect.description: If true, auto-connect ports on startup using jack_connect (requires jack_control or external script).

post_start_commands.description: Shell commands to run after JACK starts successfully (e.g., connecting clients). One command per list item.

items.description: A shell command to execute after JACK starts.
